drills.stem: A copper branch circuit is protected by a 60A OCPD. Describe the correct METHOD to find the minimum EGC.
choices: Enter Table 250.122 at the 60A OCPD row and read the copper column
Enter Table 250.66 at the 60A row and read the copper column
Read Table 310.16 at the conductor's ampacity
Match the EGC to the ungrounded conductor size
hintLadder: Primary noun: the EGC row is chosen by the OCPD rating, not the conductor
Cite: Table 250.122, OCPD row, copper column. Read the size in your book

drills.stem: The same circuit is wired with aluminum conductors. Which COLUMN of Table 250.122 applies?
choices: The aluminum or copper-clad aluminum column
Either column, the material does not change the EGC
hintLadder: Primary noun: conductor MATERIAL selects the column, aluminum here
Cite: Table 250.122 has separate copper vs aluminum/copper-clad-aluminum columns. Read the aluminum column value in your book

drills.stem: Is the Table 250.122 EGC sized from the conductor's ampacity or from something else? Pick the correct METHOD.
choices: From the ampacity of the ungrounded conductor in Table 310.16
From the rating of the OCPD ahead of the circuit, via Table 250.122
From the load calculation in Article 220
hintLadder: Primary noun: the sizing INPUT is the overcurrent device rating, not the wire's ampacity
Tab family: 250.122 EGC (then check the notes below the table)
Cite: Table 250.122 keyed to the OCPD rating. Read the table notes for parallel-conductor cases. Verify in your book
